dishes.name: Pork, Fennel & Lemon Ragù with Pappardelle
dishes.summary: A bright white ragù of oven-braised, shredded pork shoulder with fennel, lemon and Pecorino Romano, emulsified with pasta water and a little cream and tossed with pappardelle.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview A bright, aromatic white ragù built around pork shoulder, fennel, lemon, and Pecorino Romano — tender shredded pork against soft pappardelle, with fennel fronds providing aromatic lift at service. ## Yield & Timing Yield: 3–4 servings · Total: ~3½ hr · Active: ~55–60 min · Oven: 300°F / 150°C ## Prep Phase 1. Finely chop onion and fennel bulb. 2. Mince garlic and thyme. 3. Finely chop fennel fronds; reserve separately. 4. Zest and juice the lemons separately. Divide zest: reserve 25% for plating; set aside 75% for the sauce. 5. Pat pork completely dry with paper towels. ## Active Cooking **Workflow summary:** Dutch oven runs two sequential fond builds before deglazing — transfer base mixture to a bowl between phases so the pan is clear for the pork sear. ### Phase 1 — Build the Base 1. Heat Dutch oven over medium-high heat. 2. Add pancetta and ⅔ cup / 160 ml water. Cook until water evaporates and pancetta renders, *8–10 min.* 3. Continue until *golden fond develops on the base.* 4. Add onion and fennel. Cook until softened and *lightly browned, 7–10 min.* 5. Add garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper. Cook 30 seconds. Transfer mixture to a bowl. ### Phase 2 — Moderate Pork Sear 1. Return Dutch oven to medium-high heat. 2. Confirm pork is completely dry before adding to pan. 3. Sear pork pieces until *lightly browned on all sides.* Develop moderate color only — avoid a dark crust. Remove pork. ### Phase 3 — Deglaze and Braise 1. Add wine. Scrape up fond and reduce by roughly half. 2. Return vegetable mixture. Add chicken stock and water. 3. Return pork. Bring to a simmer. 4. Cover and transfer to oven. Cook at 300°F / 150°C for approximately 2½ hours. *Doneness: pork shreds easily with light fork pressure; muscle groups separate without resistance.* ### Phase 4 — Develop the Sauce 1. Remove pork to a plate. Cover Dutch oven and let stand 10–15 min so sidewall fond softens. 2. Scrape all fond into the sauce. 3. Shred pork into bite-sized pieces. Return pork and accumulated juices to the Dutch oven. ### Phase 5 — Build Final Flavor 1. Stir in 75% of the lemon zest and all of the lemon juice. Bring to a gentle simmer. 2. Assess consistency. *Target: ragù should appear slightly too loose — almost stew-like. If it already heavily coats a spoon or sits in thick ridges, loosen with a splash of stock or water before proceeding.* ### Phase 6 — Cook Pasta 1. Bring 4 quarts / 3.8 L water to a boil. Add 1 tbsp kosher salt. 2. Cook pappardelle until al dente — typically 30–60 seconds beyond package timing for dried. 3. Reserve 2 cups / 475 ml pasta water. Drain. ### Phase 7 — Finish Keep Dutch oven over **low heat** throughout this phase. 1. Add pasta to the ragù. 2. Add 1 cup / 240 ml reserved pasta water. 3. Add 70% of the Pecorino. Toss until fully emulsified. 4. Assess consistency — add additional pasta water if needed. 5. Stir in heavy cream. Toss 30–60 seconds. 6. Final consistency check — add additional pasta water if required. *Target: sauce coats pasta fluidly and pools lightly at the bottom of the bowl. It should not cling heavily.* ## Holding & Assembly 1. Remove from heat. Rest 1–2 minutes only. 2. Divide among warm bowls. 3. Garnish with reserved lemon zest and fennel fronds. 4. Serve remaining Pecorino at the table. Serve immediately. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
CriticalSauce over-reduced before pasta enters — sits in thick ridges and barely flows when spoon is dragged through itLoosen with stock, water, or pasta water before adding pasta
CriticalPork under-braised — resists shredding or pulls into long tough strandsReturn to oven until it shreds easily with light fork pressure
MajorModerate sear exceeded — dark crust and deeply roasted fondProceed; dish remains serviceable
MajorPecorino clumps — cheese forms strings rather than emulsifyingAdd warm pasta water gradually while tossing
MinorLemon dominates — acidity overwhelms pork and fennelAdjust with pasta water before considering additional cream
## Adjustment Notes Add salt only after Pecorino is incorporated. Correct texture with pasta water, not cream — pasta water is the primary finishing lever throughout. Increase richness with additional Pecorino before increasing cream. Use reserved lemon zest at plating for brightness; additional lemon juice only at service.
